notes: Read SKILL.md and 01_rbac_implementation.md, 02_permissions.md, 03_ownership.md, 04_auth_testing.md in full. The skill provides prompt templates and inline TypeScript patterns for role-based access control, granular permissions, ownership checks, and authorization testing in a Next.js + Clerk (+ Convex) app, stressing server-side checks, default deny, and negative tests.

Following it makes the agent create or modify authorization code in the user's project (middleware.ts, lib/rbac.ts, admin endpoints) and optionally curl the user's localhost app with placeholder bearer tokens (04_auth_testing.md:85-97). No installs, secret handling, or remote services.

Template dependence: written for the Secure Vibe Coding OS starter and its files (@middleware.ts, @convex/http.ts, @lib/clerk.ts at 01_rbac_implementation.md:90-93), but the templates describe what to build (lib/rbac.ts, role utilities, webhook role assignment) and the core patterns are given inline in SKILL.md:300-503, so they work in any Next.js + Clerk project. Pointers to sibling skills (prompt-engineering, threat-modeling) and `.claude/skills/security/...` install paths are optional.

Minor technical caveats: reading `sessionClaims.publicMetadata.role` requires customizing the Clerk session token to include public metadata; newer Clerk versions make `auth()` async; `Response.redirect("/unauthorized")` at SKILL.md:324 needs an absolute URL. None of these weaken the security guidance.
